title: Void Ending in an Opposition to Mars
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The opposition is the hardest figure the Moon can close on: the text grades it as extreme enmity, because the signs it joins stand opposed across all four natural qualities. It shares with the square the warnings that guard every election, and a Moon waning in light and faced by Saturn is the source's own example of a serious misfortune.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with an opposition to Mars, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his fire and his knife. Mars is the planet of the knife and the forge: surgery, bloodletting, the taming of wild beasts, the smithy's fire, war, and banditry fall under him, with army camps, battlefields, and places of judgment among his locations. His seat in the body is the gallbladder, the source of yellow bile and heat, and bright red is his color. A waxing Moon facing him by aspect is counted a misfortune; his is the figure the lunar doctrine watches hardest.
